ownership.quote: The company went public on the New York Stock Exchange in 2019 under the ticker symbol NET.

stage.quote: On August 15, 2019, Cloudflare submitted its S-1 filing for an initial public offering on the New York Stock Exchange under the stock ticker NET. It opened for public trading on September 13, 2019, at $15 per share.
stage.note: Workers for Platforms is a paid add-on product on top of the Workers platform, not a separately funded entity; Cloudflare itself is a public company (NYSE: NET) since 2019.

total_funding_usd.basis: Crunchbase-aggregated pre-IPO venture funding total for Cloudflare, Inc. across seed through Series E rounds (2010-2019); no single primary source confirms the exact sum.
total_funding_usd.quote: In 2009, the company was venture-capital funded.

last_round.quote: Cloudflare's $150 million funding round puts its IPO plans in question

revenue.basis: Cloudflare, Inc. 2025 Annual Report (Form 10-K), total company revenue; not broken out per-product (Workers for Platforms revenue is not separately disclosed).

note: Cloudflare (NYSE: NET) is a public company; Workers for Platforms is a product/pricing tier within Cloudflare's Workers developer platform, not a separately financed company, so funding/stage fields reflect Cloudflare, Inc. as a whole and revenue is company-wide (per-product revenue not disclosed). In May 2026 Cloudflare cut ~1,100 jobs (~20% of workforce) despite record quarterly revenue, per TechCrunch, citing AI-driven role obsolescence.
